questions.question: Which of the following vitamins helps to keep our skin and eyes healthy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vitamin A:**
 
• This vitamin is crucial for maintaining the health of both your skin and eyes.
 
• It is a fat-soluble vitamin that plays an essential role in ensuring normal vision.
 
• It produces pigments in the retina of the eye and promotes good vision, especially in low light.
 
• It also helps the heart, lungs, kidneys, and other organs function properly.
 
• Moreover, it is involved in the regulation of the immune system.
 
• For the skin, vitamin A helps to speed up healing, prevent breakouts, and support the skin's immune system, promoting natural moisturising.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
 

 Vitamin
 Role in Skin Health
 Role in Eye Health
 
 

 Vitamin C
 As an antioxidant, helps to protect the skin from damaging free radicals caused by UV exposure. Aids in the skin's natural regeneration process and helps prevent dry skin.
 Supports the health of blood vessels in the eye and might decrease the risk of cataracts.
 
 

 Vitamin D
 May contribute to skin health by managing the growth of cells and reducing inflammation.
 Some research points to vitamin D deficiency being associated with an increased risk of age-related macular degeneration, but its role in eye health is less established.
 
 

 
 Vitamin B (B3, B5, B7, B2, B6, B9, B12)

 

 

 

 
 
 B3 and B5 improve skin hydration, reduce redness and inflammation, and boost skin elasticity. B7 promotes healthy hair, skin, and nails. 
 B2 helps prevent cataracts. A combination of B6, B9, and B12 might reduce the risk of age-related macular degeneration.

questions.question: According to the 2011 census, what is the literacy rate of New Delhi District?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 88.01 percent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the 2011 census, the literacy rate of the New Delhi district was 88.01 percent.
 
• This figure combines the literacy rates of both males and females in the district.
 
• Literacy rates can change over time due to various factors such as government initiatives, societal changes, and improvements in education infrastructure, among others. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Motto of the census of India 2011 was 'Our Census, Our Future'.
 
• It was the 15th term that was conducted by the Ministry of Home Affairs regarding census in India.
 
• The census of India was conducted in the two phases first in House listing and second phase in Population counting.
 
• According to the Census reports on 31 March 2011, the Population of India has increased to 1.21 billion with a Decadal Growth of 17.70 percent of the total population. 
 
• The Adult Literacy Rate has increased to 74.04% with a Decadal Growth of 9.21%. 
 
• The Indian Government decided in May 1949 to initiate steps for Developing a Systematic collection of Statistics Data on the size of the Population and its Growth Rate.
 
• So it established an Organisation in the Ministry of Home Affairs under the name of Registrar General and Ex-Officio Census Commissioner.
 
• Registrar General office founded in the year 1961 under the Home ministry in India.
 
• The rank of Registrar is usually held by a Civil Servant He/ She must be holding the rank of the Joint Secretary level.

questions.question: India accounts for what percent of total geographical area of the world?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **2.4 percent**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India accounts for approximately 2.4 percent of the total geographical area of the world. 
 
• India is the seventh-largest country in the world in terms of geographical area.
 
• It is situated in South Asia.
 
• India shares its borders with Pakistan to the northwest, China and Nepal to the north, Bhutan to the northeast, and Bangladesh and Myanmar to the east. To the south, it is bounded by the Indian Ocean.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Geographically, India is extremely diverse, featuring a wide range of climate regions and landscapes.
 
• Here are some of the main geographical features:
 
 
• **The Himalayas: **
 
• This mountain range in the north serves as a natural barrier between India and the Tibetan Plateau.
 
• Mount Kanchenjunga, located on the border between India and Nepal, is the highest point in India.
 
• **The Northern Plains:**
 
• Also known as the Indo-Gangetic Plains, this region was formed by the basin of the Indus, Ganga (Ganges), and Brahmaputra rivers.
 
• It's one of the world's most fertile and densely populated areas.
 
• **The Thar Desert:**
 
• Located in the northwestern part of India, it's the world's 17th largest desert and the ninth largest subtropical desert.
 
• **The Deccan Plateau:**
 
• This large plateau in southern India is elevated and characterized by rolling hills and valleys.
 
• **The Ghats: **
 
• The Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats are mountain ranges that run parallel to India's western and eastern coasts, respectively.
 
• **Coastal Plains:**
 
• India has extensive coastal plains on both its eastern and western coasts.
 
• The western coastal plains are narrower, while the eastern coastal plains are broader and more fertile.
 
• **Islands: **
 
• India has two major island groups – the Andaman and Nicobar Islands in the Bay of Bengal and the Lakshadweep Islands in the Arabian Sea.

questions.question: Which among the following substances is used in moisturizing creams and soaps because of its hygroscopic properties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Glycerol**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Glycerol** is used in moisturizing creams and soaps because of its hygroscopic properties.
 
• **Glycerol (also known as Glycerin):** It is used in moisturizers, soaps, and a variety of other personal care products due to its hygroscopic properties, meaning it can attract and hold water molecules from the environment.
 
• This property makes it a good ingredient for hydrating and moisturizing the skin.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Galena: **This is a lead sulfide mineral and the most important ore of lead. It's not used in cosmetics due to its lead content, which can be toxic.
 
• **Ethanol:** Also known as ethyl alcohol, it's a common ingredient in many cosmetic and beauty products due to its versatility as an antibacterial, a solvent, and in some cases, an astringent. However, it's not specifically known for its hygroscopic properties.
 
• **Freon:** This is a brand name for a type of chlorofluorocarbon (CFC) used primarily as a refrigerant. It's not used in cosmetics.

questions.question: Who among the following has been awarded with Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award 2021 for "Para Shooting"?

The correct answer is __**Avani Lekhara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Avani Lekhara

 
 
• Avani Lekhara, an Indian Paralympian and rifle shooter, was born on November 8, 2001.
 
• At the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, she earned a Gold Medal in the 10m air rifle standing event and a Bronze Medal in the 50m rifle three positions event.
 
• In 2022, Avani Lekhara receives the Padma Shri award from former President Ram Nath Kovind.
 
• She is the first Indian woman to win two medals in the same Paralympics and the country's first gold medalist.

• The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports distributes it every year.
 
• Chess Grandmaster Viswanathan Anand was the first recipient for this award, recognized for his efforts in the academic year 1991–1992.

questions.question: The prehistoric period in the early development of human beings is commonly known as the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Old stone age**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The earliest age in history is called Old Stone Age or Palaeolithic.
 
• It is roughly taken as 2.5 million years ago to 10,000 B.C.
 
• It is characterized by the use of rudimentary chipped stone tools.
 
• Early development of human beings started during this period.
 
• This period is divided into
 
 
• Lower Palaeolithic culture
 
• Middle Palaeolithic culture
 
• Upper Palaeolithic culture
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Neolithic period marked the beginning of agriculture and animal domestication.
 
• The site of Mehrgarh has produced evidence of early Neolithic times, dating to 7000 BCE.
 
• The Chalcolithic or Copper Age is the transitional period between the Neolithic and the Bronze Age.
 
• The period of the Copper Age was from 1800 BC - 800 BC.
 
• The presence of painted pottery is a hallmark of the Chalcolithic period.

questions.question: Which among the following is NOT a Jovian planet?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mercury**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first four planets are called Terrestrial, meaning earth-like planets like Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars.
 
• **They are also called inner planets.
 
• They lie between the sun and the belt of asteroids.
 
• They are made up of rock and metals and have relatively high densities.
 
• The terrestrial planets were formed in the close vicinity of the parent star where it was too warm for gases to condense to solid particles.
 
• The terrestrial planets are smaller and their lower gravity could not hold the escaping gases. 
 
• Other than them the planets are called jovian or giant planets like Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.
 
 
• They are also called the outer planets.
 
• Most of them are much larger than the terrestrial planets and have a thick atmosphere, mostly of helium and hydrogen.
 
• The solar winds were not all that intense to cause the removal of gases from the Jovian planets.​ 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

questions.question: Article 17 of the Indian constitution is related with ______.
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __Abolition of Untouchability__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Fundamental Rights from articles 12-35 have been classified under six categories:

 
 
• Right to Freedom​
 
• Right to Equality
 
• Right against Exploitation
 
• Right to Freedom of Religion
 
• Cultural and Educational rights
 
• Right to constitutional remedies
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Article 14 - Equality before the law
 
• Article 15 - Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• Article 16 - Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment
 
• Article 17 - Abolition of Untouchability
 
• Article 18 - Abolition of titles
 
• Article 19 - Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.
 
• Article 20 and 21 are the two articles (Fundamental Rights) of the Indian Constitution that are not suspended even during the National Emergency under Article 359.
 
• Article 20 gives protection in respect of conviction for offenses.
 
• Article 21 gives the right to life, personal liberty, and the right to die with dignity.
 
• Article 21A gives free education to all children aged, six to fourteen(6-14) years.

questions.question: Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam, famous Indian scientist's, autobiography is known as _______.

• It was written by Dr. Abdul Kalam and Arun Tiwari.
 
• Dr. Kalam examines his early life, effort, hardship, fortitude, luck, and the chance that eventually led him to lead Indian space research, nuclear and missile programs.
 
• It was originally published in 1999.
 
• The complete name of A P J Abdul Kalam is Avul Pakir Jainulabdeen Abdul Kalam.
 
• He was an Indian aerospace scientist and politician.
 
• He served as the 11th President of India from 2002 to 2007. 
 
• He was also known as the Missile Man of India for his work on the development of ballistic missile and launch vehicle technology.
 
• He was widely referred to as the "People's President".
 
• 
 
**One Life is Not Enough: An Autobiography by Natwar Singh**

 
 
• ** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**
 
 

 **Brief Intro:** This autobiography is written by K. Natwar Singh, an Indian politician and former diplomat. Published in 2014, the book provides insights into Natwar Singh's political career, his experiences in the Indian Foreign Service, and his time as India's Minister of External Affairs. It also delves into various aspects of his personal life and his reflections on Indian politics.

 
 
• 
 
**Waiting for a Visa by B.R. Ambedkar**

 
**Brief Intro:** Written by B.R. Ambedkar, a prominent Indian jurist, social reformer, and the chief architect of the Indian Constitution, "Waiting for a Visa" is a collection of autobiographical writings. The book provides a glimpse into Ambedkar's early life, his struggles against social discrimination, and his quest for education. It sheds light on the challenges faced by the marginalized communities in India.

Published in 2013, the book narrates Milkha Singh's journey from his childhood in undivided India to becoming one of the country's most celebrated sports figures. questions.question: The Delhi Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Bill 2022 aimed at unifying the _______ Municipal Corporations of Delhi to ensure a robust setup for synergised and strategic planning and optimal utilisation of resources.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Parliament has passed the Delhi Municipal Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2022.
 
• The Bill seeks to further amend the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957, and proposes to unify the three existing Municipal Corporations of Delhi into one Municipal Corporation of Delhi.
 
• It also limits the number of councilors from 272 to a maximum of 250.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The bill envisages bringing about greater transparency, improved governance, and more efficient delivery of civic service for the people of Delhi.
 
• At present, the three corporations in Delhi, North, South, and East Delhi Municipal Corporations, have a total of 272 seats.
 
• While North and South corporations have 104 wards each, the East Corporation has 64 wards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Galvanization is the process of applying a coating of zinc to steel or iron. 
 
• This is done to protect steel and iron from the process of rusting.
 
• The most common method of galvanization is " hot-dip-galvanization".
 
• In this method, parts are submerged in a bath of molten hot zinc.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When zinc is coated on iron or steel, it protects corrosive substances from reaching the underlying steel or iron. 
 
• The electroplating such as chromate conversion coating is applied to provide further surface passivation to the substrate material.
 
• The hot-dipping method is not applicable to materials that are constantly exposed to acid and acid rains.
 
• It is also applicable to bolts and nuts.

questions.question: Which among the following is the famous harvest festival of Meghalaya, India?

questions.question: Bharatanatyam dance is associated with which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

__
 
• **Bharatanatyam **is one of the** oldest classical dance traditions in India, **originating in **Tamil Nadu.**
 
• It is **characterized by its distinct hand gestures (mudras), facial expressions (abhinaya), footwork, and sophisticated choreography that combine to express a story or theme.**
 
• The dance form was** traditionally performed in temples by the Devadasis (servant of the deity) and later started to be performed in royal courts.**
 
• Bharatanatyam includes three aspects - **Nritta (pure dance), Nritya (solo expressive dance), and Natya (group dramatic dance).**
 
• It is a **highly spiritual and dedicatory dance form that aims to connect the performer and audience with the divine.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Indian Railways plan to become Net Zero Carbon Emitter by ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __1.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• Indian Railways is moving towards becoming the world’s largest green railway network by achieving “net-zero carbon emission” by 2030.
 
• **To achieve the same, it has taken some of the following steps:**
 
 
• The Railways plans to electrify balance Broad Gauge (BG) routes by December 2023 to achieve 100% electrification of BG routes.
 
• It also plans to have Head-On-Generation systems, Bio-Toilets and LED lights. 
 
• The Railways dedicated Freight Corridors are being developed as a low-carbon green transportation network with a long-term low-carbon roadmap.
 
• The Green certifications are allotted keeping in mind the sustainable development goals such as the use of renewable energy.
 
• The Indian Railways has also built solar-powered stations to contribute towards environmental protection.
 
• The Indian Railways has also incorporated Climate Change features in its own risk assessments and disaster management protocols.

questions.question: What does 'F' stand for in FRBM Act, 2003 of Indian economy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fiscal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The full form of the **FRBM Act is the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act.**
 
• The** 'F' in FRBM stands for Fiscal, **referring to government revenue, spending, and debt.
 
• The act was legislated by the **Government of India in 2003 to ensure fiscal discipline in the country.**
 
• The FRBM Act aims to eliminate revenue deficit and bring down fiscal deficit.
 
• This is achieved by** setting targets for the government's fiscal indicators like revenue deficit, fiscal deficit, and debt.**
 
• The act also restricts the government from borrowing from the **Reserve Bank of India, thereby ensuring financial stability.**
 
• The act encourages transparent **fiscal management systems in the country.**
 
• By **maintaining fiscal discipline, the act helps in controlling inflation and promoting economic stability.**

questions.question: Who among the following introduced the silver tanka and the copper Jital - the two basic coins of the Sultanate period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Iltumish.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Iltutmish **introduced the** Silver Tanka and Copper Jital, the two coins of the Delhi Sultanate.**
 
• The coins prior to Iltutmish were** introduced by the Rulers which bear the Sanskrit characters and even Bull and Shivalinga.**
 
• Iltutmish was the first to introduce a **“Pure Arabic Coin” in India.**
 
• The Coins were engraved with** “The Mighty Sultan, Sun of the Empire and the Faith, Conquest-laden, Iltumish,”** after he received an investiture of **Sovereign Sultan of Delhi from the Caliph of Baghdad.**
 
• The Silver Tanka issued by **Iltutmish was weighing 175 grains.**
 
• **Gold Tanka **of the same** weight was later issued by Balban.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which of the following states is the leading producer of cotton in India, as of November 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Gujarat__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Gujarat is the leading producer of cotton__.

 __
 
• Gujarat is the largest producer of cotton in India because its climatic and geographical conditions are ideal for cotton production are suitable for cotton cultivation.
 
• Kanam province of Bharuch in Gujarat is well known for the production of the best quality.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• In India, cotton is grown in **9 major cotton-growing States **viz. Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan in the Northern zone, **Gujarat, Maharashtra and MP in Central zone and Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu in the Southern zone.**
 
• Besides, cotton is also grown in Orissa.
 
• West Bengal is the largest producer of rice in India.
 
 
• Rice production for the state totalled 14.99 million tonnes in 2017-18. West Bengal is also a major producer of fish.
 
 
 
• Assam is the single largest tea-producing region globally and contributes over 50% to India's total tea production.
 
 
• It is the largest producer of ginger, second largest producer of pineapple, and third-largest producer of okra and areca nut, amongst Indian states.
 
 
 
• Odisha is the leading producer of chromite, graphite, bauxite, manganese ore, iron ore, sillimanite, quartzite, pyroxenite and dolomite.
 
 
• The State hosts the country's sole resources of ruby and platinum group of metals.

questions.question: Who was the President of Swaraj Party formed in the year 1923?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chittaranjan Das**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Swaraj Party was established on 1 January 1923 by Chittaranjan Das and Motilal Nehru.
 
• The two important leaders of the Party were CR Das and Motilal Nehru in which CR Das was the President and Motilal Nehru was its secretary.
 
• The Party was established as the Congress Khilafat Swaraj Party.
 
• The Swaraj Party sought greater self-government and political freedom from the British Raj for the Indian people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In 1923, The Swaraj Party won the most seats during elections to the Bengal Legislative Council.
 
• Important leaders of the Swaraj Party included Huseyn Shaheed Suhrawardy, N C Kelkar, and Subhas Chandra Bose.
 
• In 1925, Swarajist Vithalbhai Patel became the speaker of the Central Legislative Assembly.
 
• This is the main achievement of the Party.
